newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel braces for unrest, sees summit with PLO.
newsitem.headline: Israel braces for unrest, sees summit with PLO.

text.p: Israel's Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said on Monday he had reinforced troops in the West Bank and Gaza Strip to pre-empt Palestinian unrest when construction on a new Jewish settlement begins this week.
He spoke to Israel Radio as Israeli officials said they expected to arrange a summit this week with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to discuss the tension spawned by the settlement plans.
"I ordered the deployment of forces starting today along a very wide perimeter in the Gaza Strip, the West Bank and along the seam (dividing Israel from the West Bank and Gaza)," he said.
Israel's decision to build 6,500 houses in Arab East Jerusalem for Jews has angered Palestinians who say the move violates Israel-PLO peace deals.

Israeli security officials have warned that the start of construction could spark violence similiar to clashes last September that claimed the lives of 61 Palestinians and 15 Israeli soldiers when Israel punched an opening in a tunnel in East Jerusalem near key Islamic sites.
"Our working assumption is that incidents are likely to occur, even severe incidents. For this reason we have deployed our forces," Mordechai said.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy said he expected a summit between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Arafat would take place this week.
Netanyahu spoke by phone with Arafat on Sunday after Palestinians severed contacts over the Jewish state's decision to build the new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Israel, which captured East Jerusalem in the 1967 Middle East War, views it as part of its capital. Palestinians want that half of the city as the capital of a future state. Its future is supposed to be negotiated.

Netanyahu said he hoped the conversation, brokered by Jordan's King Hussein during a visit to Israel, would put the Israeli-PLO dialogue on a new footing. But he also vowed Israel would break ground this week for the Jabal Abu Ghneim settlement -- Har Homa in Hebrew.
Israeli security sources said Netanyahu's cabinet secretary Danny Naveh would meet PLO negotiator Saeb Erekat at 2 p.m. (1200 GMT) to try to arrange the summit.
A meeting between Mordechai and Palestinian Authority member Nabil Shaath was also scheduled on Monday.
Talks have been suspended since the PLO rejected an Israeli interim withdrawal plan from the West Bank earlier this month which fell far short of its expectations.

In a gesture to the Palestinians, Netanyahu said Israel would let Arafat use the Gaza Strip airport of Dahanya and an agreement on that might be signed on Monday. Full operation of the airport is still not agreed.

King Hussein visited Israel to console families of seven schoolgirls shot dead by one of his soldiers at the border last week and to defuse tensions with Netanyahu over a harsh letter he wrote to the prime minister over his settlement plans.
Officials on Amman said Jordan's Crown Prince Hassan would travel to Gaza on Monday to meet Arafat.
